svg.text: Timetable System - Users & Goals x Tech Stack
Who uses it, what they need, and which part of the tech stack serves each need. Final product: open source, self-hosted by any institution in the country.
Builds the timetable for the chosen years, once per term
Runs the teacher availability round, approves changes,
Uses: every page of the web app
Gives busy times, subjects they can teach, max hours/day
Sees ONLY their own timetable, sends change requests
Enters rooms shared by several departments
Same as a department head, in their own profiles
Their published timetables book shared rooms
Students (NOT a user - no account, ever)
Receive the published timetable of their group
as an A4 print or file
3 days - 1 week per term, mostly teachers negotiating
Changes keep coming after the 'final' table
what each user needs to get done
For every group in the chosen years
G2 Much faster than 3 days - 1 week
Target: under 30 min of work, then as fast as possible
Move classes, pin agreed ones, Schedule / Reserve electives
G4 Trust the data from the PDF
See and fix what was read before it spreads
College name, group, subject list, weekly grid
Busy times and preferred subjects are used by the solver
I1 Admin: no double-booked shared rooms
N1 change a timetable without the user asking
N2 show teachers' data outside the institution
from tech-stack-list.txt - what each part is used for
All pages: profile manager, review, arrange (drag & drop),
project service - FastAPI (the ONLY writer of data)
Profiles, availability rounds, change requests, versions, change log
import service - pdftotext + curriculum format readers
Reads the PDF into subjects; every value keeps its PDF page
Places classes in < 1 s; pins; N candidates; partial result + tray
Teacher rules = CORE (busy times, max hours)
core lib - Python rules, pre-check, rule checker
Explains impossible cases before running; re-checks every result;
answers the live check on each drop (POST /api/check)
storage - JSON files now -> PostgreSQL (Docker, later)
Profiles, rooms, teachers, runs; stays on the institution's server
docker compose up; one-command update; HTTPS, backups, PDPA
Roles: institution admin, head, teacher (no student)
Email only if the admin sets a mail server: invites, deadlines, changes
BELONGS TO BOTH - a user need that also needs a specific tech piece
Tags (G1, T1, N2 ...) link a user or tech part to the goal it serves
